title: Controlled localization of anyons in a graphene quantum Hall interferometer
claims: A gate-controlled anti-dot inside a bilayer-graphene Fabry-Pérot interferometer produces hundreds of reproducible, discrete phase slips in five fractional quantum Hall states.
The interfering edge carries charge equal to the fractional part of the cavity filling, e.g. e/2 at 1+1/2 and 2e/5 at -2/5, from the Aharonov-Bohm periodicity.
For the abelian states 1+1/3 and -2/5, the slip sizes (about 1/3 and 1/5 of 2π) agree with the expected braiding phases of single e/3 and e/5 quasiparticles entering the anti-dot.
At 1+1/2, the slips indicate that putative non-abelian e/4 quasiparticles are loaded one by one into the anti-dot, a step toward non-abelian braiding.
Slip spacing and slip counting, combined with the anti-dot radius, give fractional localized charges and exclude charge e.
Slip regions recur once per anti-dot Landau level, with an ordering that tracks the cavity filling, pointing to reconstructed anti-dot edges.
summary: The authors etch a hole in the top graphite gate of a bilayer-graphene Fabry-Pérot interferometer and tune the enclosed anti-dot with a bridge gate, observing long series of discrete interference phase slips at ν = -1/2, -2/5, -1/3, 1+1/3 and 1+1/2. They interpret the slips as single fractional quasiparticles entering the anti-dot and extract braiding phases of about 1/3, 1/5 and 1/4 (in units of 2π), presenting the last as controlled localization of putative non-abelian e/4 anyons.
strengths: A new and useful device concept: a bridge-gated anti-dot inside a graphite-gated bilayer-graphene interferometer gives gate control of the localized quasiparticle population rather than relying on random traps.
Clean Aharonov-Bohm interference in five fractional states, including two even-denominator states, with interfering charges consistent with the fractional part of the filling (Fig. 1d-f).

The slips recur at the same bridge-gate voltage over 50 repeated sweeps (Ext. Fig. 6) and group into three anti-dot filling windows per state whose ordering follows the cavity filling (Fig. 4b), at two magnetic fields (Ext. Fig. 8).
Capacitance-based charge estimates rule out charge e entering the anti-dot, and self-consistent COMSOL/Thomas-Fermi electrostatics support the parallel-plate estimate of the anti-dot filling.

issues.issue: The sawtooth of a large negative inter-slip slope plus positive jumps is the generic signature of a charging island capacitively coupled to the interfering edge, where the jump is θ_a minus a non-universal coupling term that can be as large as the jump. The paper invokes such coupling for the smaller jumps but assumes the prominent ones carry the bare θ_a, and the small-ζ conclusion of Methods D concerns cavity bulk-edge coupling, not AD-to-edge coupling.

Fit a model with AD-edge and bulk-edge coupling, report how far Δθ_ps can be pulled from θ_a, and explain why coupling is negligible for the prominent jumps only.

issues.claim: Slips come from quasiparticles entering the AD
issues.headline: No integer-filling or pre-etch controls where statistical phase is trivial
issues.issue: At integer cavity filling, electrons entering the AD give a trivial 2π phase, so any visible slip would measure pure Coulomb or coupling effects; similar controls are an integer ν_AD window, a depleted or far-off-plateau hole region, and data taken before the hole was etched. Without them, a jump of about 1/3 cannot be separated from coupling-induced jumps or electrostatic artifacts at the bridge-gate overhang, which also tunes the area.

issues.fix: Show the same V_brg-V_TG maps and step analysis at integer ν_cav under the AD conditions of Figs. 2-4, for an integer ν_AD, and from before the hole was etched, reporting whether slips appear and how large they are.
issues.fix_scoped: These observations are consistent with the AD filling with quasiparticles one-by-one, although without integer-filling control measurements we cannot exclude electrostatic contributions to the slips.

edit_scoped.after: These observations are consistent with the AD filling with quasiparticles one-by-one, although without integer-filling control measurements we cannot exclude electrostatic contributions to the slips.

issues.headline: e/4 charge with e/2 interferer does not test non-abelian statistics
issues.issue: With an abelian e/2 interferer, the expected slip reduces to the localized charge, so the measurement probes only the charge-sector phase, which is the same for Pfaffian, anti-Pfaffian and abelian candidates such as 331 or K = 8, and no even-odd effect can appear. The abstract and conclusion nevertheless read as evidence of non-abelian loading.

issues.fix: State that the data fix the localized charge and abelian mutual statistics but not non-abelian character, list the compatible candidate orders, temper the milestone and qubit language, and discuss or attempt the parity-dependent e/4 interference test this AD enables.

issues.claim: Charge needed to destabilize AD order
issues.headline: Destabilization-charge statement is suggestive but not quantified
issues.issue: The statement that the charge needed to destabilize the AD topological order roughly equals the charge forming it is suggestive but not quantified.

issues.fix: Either support the statement quantitatively or soften it.
